label: Content-fixed favouring: a re-description is not an outcome-independent selector
paraphrase: Analyst formulation on any local STIT frame with an outcome map, where an explanatory level supplies a content at each history and each content has a favouring relation on outcomes; the level explains 'the actual outcome rather than y' when its actual content favours the actual outcome over y (pro tanto; the cell-carrier analogue of SELECTING_AN_OUTCOME_1, not one of its senses and not bridged to it). (1) If the content is the same at every compared history and its favouring relations are asymmetric (net favouring; a content with pro tanto reasons in both directions is outside this law), then with a contingent outcome it does not favour each history's outcome over every other realized outcome at every history. (2) The outcome itself, as content favouring itself over everything else, does that at every history, has asymmetric favouring, and with a contingent outcome is not the same at every history. (3) A content constant on the cells of a single-cell (invariant) level is the same at every history. (4) A content that favours only what a standard G ranks higher does not select the actual outcome when another realized outcome is not ranked below it by G. (5) With an asymmetric G under which every realized outcome is bettered by a realized outcome, no such content selects. Law 1 excludes every outcome-independent asymmetric content equally, so it does not discriminate among accounts; at the actual history alone, the re-description is excluded by the admission condition (outcome independence), not by law 1. Nothing about rationality, chance or goodness beyond the named relations is typed.
